roles: exchange interior reachability and hop-count distance information among routers
addressing: RFC 1058-generation route representation follows the classful IPv4 era; later RIP-2 revisions add additional capabilities.
routing_or_forwarding: Distance-vector/Bellman-Ford family with hop-count metric and bounded infinity.

operations.monitoring: Routing-table and neighbor update observation is implementation-specific.
operations.diagnostics: Count-to-infinity, route aging and update propagation are key operational behaviors.
operations.failure_behavior: Topology changes propagate through periodic/triggered distance-vector updates with convergence limitations characteristic of the family.

survival.provenance_notes: RIP remains present in legacy/small systems; historical implementation lineage requires separate source records.

open_questions: Recover RIP ancestry before RFC 1058 and document links to Xerox/PUP/XNS and Unix routed only where primary evidence supports them.
Recover early routed source versions and vendor implementations.

related_artifacts.notes: OSPF occupies the same IGP role but uses a different link-state/SPF algorithmic family.
Integrated IS-IS is another parallel IGP family with different standards ancestry.

notes: Do not encode RIP→OSPF or RIP→IS-IS as a formal revision chain.
